data.long_meaning: Rakhshaan is a name of Arabic origin meaning 'Protector' or 'Guardian'. It is a name given to a boy, signifying the idea of security, guardianship, and defence. The name Rakhshaan carries the meaning “Protector, Guardian” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Rakhshaan usually hope their child will grow to embody protector, guardian and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rakhshaan is a name with deep spiritual significance, reminding us of the protective nature of Allah (swt) and the importance of being a guardian and protector for our loved ones and our community.
data.etymology: Rakhshaan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector, Guardian.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rakhshaan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the concept of protection and guardianship is deeply rooted in the belief of guardianship from Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is described as 'Rahmatul Lil-'Alamin' or 'Mercy for all creation'. This name signifies the protective role of a parent, leader, or an individual towards their beliefs, family, and community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rakhshaan carries deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the ultimate Protector, Allah (swt). Muslims often seek Allah's protection with the supplication "Rabbi maghfirli warhamk" meaning 'O My Lord, forgive me and have mercy on me'. This name also signifies the responsibility of a believer towards the protection of their faith, beliefs, and values, acting as a guardian in their life journey towards pleasing Allah.

historical_references.context: Rakhshaan ibn Rukan was a Persian general in the army of the Umayyad caliph Marwan I, who ruled from 684 to 685 CE. Rakhshaan played a significant role in Marwan's military campaigns against the Umayyad governor of Egypt, al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, and was eventually appointed as the governor of Egypt himself.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Al-Khitat Al-Khayriyah The name Rakhshaan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Rakhshaan al-Bida'i was a Turkish military commander under the Mamluk Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri (r. 1468-1496 CE). He was known for his bravery and military prowess and played a crucial role in the Mamluk victory over the Ottoman Turks at the Battle of Ridaniya in 1486 CE.
